articles.title: Read and search your email
articles.summary: Ask in plain words, by sender, subject or date. Reading never changes your mailbox.
articles.keywords: read search find list unread messages inbox summarize from subject date attachment flagged starred folder
steps: Ask for what is new, for example: "Show my unread email from today."
Describe a message by sender, recipient, subject words, dates or attachments.
Ask your assistant to keep reading when a long email stops early.
Name a folder, such as Sent or Archive, to read mail there.
Ask it to mark messages as read. Reading alone never does.

articles.title: Find messages a search missed
articles.summary: Name the folder, use whole words, and on Outlook search words and filters separately.
articles.keywords: search missing not found folder archive sent imap gmail outlook whole word trash spam filter
steps: On IMAP mailboxes, name your archive or sent folder. Only the Inbox is searched.
On Gmail and Outlook, name Trash to search it. Gmail also skips Spam.
On Gmail and Outlook, use whole words for the subject. Part words find nothing.
On Outlook, ask for words and filters like unread or dates in separate searches.
On IMAP mailboxes, the "has an attachment" filter is ignored.

articles.title: Send a new email
articles.summary: Say who to write to and what to say. A sent email cannot be taken back.
articles.keywords: send write compose new email recipient to cc bcc reply-to contact address find someone approval
steps: Ask, for example: "Email ola@example.com and ask if Thursday at 10 works."
Ask "What is Anna's email address?" to find it in your recent mail.
Add Cc, Bcc or a reply-to address. Up to 50 recipients per field.
Ask for a draft instead when you want to check it first.
If send approval is on, an owner or admin must approve it under Approvals.

articles.title: Reply to or forward an email
articles.summary: Replies stay in the conversation. Forwards arrive as the original was sent, attachments included.
articles.keywords: reply reply all respond answer forward fwd thread conversation attachments note eml
steps: Ask, for example: "Reply to Ola and say Thursday works."
Say "reply all" to include everyone. Otherwise only the sender gets it.
To forward, name the message and the new recipients, plus an optional note.
Ask to leave the attachments out, or to forward the original as an attachment.
Forward up to 50 messages to the same people in one request.

articles.title: Save an email as a draft
articles.summary: Ask for a draft to check an email first. It is saved in your mailbox's Drafts folder.
articles.keywords: draft save unsent review later edit update reply draft drafts folder
steps: Ask, for example: "Draft a reply to Ola, but do not send it."
Open it from the Drafts folder in your usual mail app, if you like.
Ask your assistant to change the text, subject or recipients, or to add files.
Ask it to send the draft when it is ready. Sending cannot be undone.
Ask it to list your drafts or delete one.

articles.title: Edit and send a draft in the chat
articles.summary: Where your AI client shows it, a prepared draft appears as a card you can edit and send.
articles.keywords: draft editor card in-chat edit send undo discard save card hide turn off show
body: Hide the card for one mailbox in its details under Inboxes, or for the whole workspace in Settings, Draft editor card.
steps: Edit the recipients, subject or text in the card, then save. Saving sends nothing.
Choose Send. Press Undo within a few seconds to keep the draft.
Use the trash icon to discard the draft at your provider.
On Gmail and IMAP mailboxes, ask your assistant to edit drafts with attachments.
To hide cards, open More options and choose Turn off draft cards…

articles.title: Send, read and save attachments
articles.summary: Attach up to 20 files (10 MB in total), read a file's text, or download files up to 25 MB.
articles.keywords: attachment attach file pdf csv download extract read size limit 10 MB 25 MB eml original
steps: Ask your assistant to attach a file to an email or draft.
Name a file already in your mailbox to send it on without uploading it again.
Ask it to read a file's text: plain text, CSV, HTML, JSON or text-layer PDFs.
Scanned images and scanned PDFs are not read.
Ask for an email's original to get the whole message as an .eml file.

articles.title: Move, archive and flag messages
articles.summary: Move, copy, archive, flag or mark messages, and manage folders. Most of it can be undone.
articles.keywords: move archive folder label flag star mark read unread copy organize sort create rename delete folder gmail labels bulk
body: Gmail uses labels: a move adds the label and takes the message out of the Inbox.
steps: Ask, for example: "Move this week's receipts to the Receipts folder."
Ask to archive, flag or unflag messages, or mark them read or unread.
Ask to move everything a search matches, up to 500 messages per request.
Ask to create, rename or delete folders. Deleting a folder cannot be undone.
Copy works everywhere except Gmail connected by signing in with Google.

articles.title: Delete email
articles.summary: Deleted mail goes to Trash. A permanent delete skips Trash and cannot be undone.
articles.keywords: delete remove trash bin permanent erase expunge bulk clean up
steps: Ask to delete a message, a list of messages, or everything a search matches.
Up to 500 messages are deleted per request.
Ask for a permanent delete only when you mean it.
Gmail connected by signing in with Google supports Trash only.
Make sure your connector or API key has the delete permission.

articles.title: Schedule an email for later
articles.summary: Name a future time and its time zone. Delivery can be up to a minute late.
articles.keywords: schedule send later delay timed future queue cancel scheduled tomorrow morning time zone
steps: Ask, for example: "Send this to Ola tomorrow at 09:00 Oslo time."
Ask "What emails are scheduled?" to see what is queued.
Ask to cancel one before it starts sending.
Give it the files directly. Files from other emails cannot be reused here.
If send approval is on, it waits under Approvals first.

articles.title: Set your signature and sender name
articles.summary: Each inbox has its own signature and sender name. Set them in Inboxes or ask your assistant.
articles.keywords: signature sign-off footer logo image sender name display name from name reply forward html
steps: In Inboxes, click the mailbox, then open Signature & sending.
Fill in Sender name and choose Save name.
Under Email signature, use Rich text or HTML source, then choose Save signature.
Under On replies & forwards, choose Always add, First reply only or Never add.
Turn on Embed images in the message if your logo does not show.

articles.title: Work with more than one inbox
articles.summary: Say which address to use. Ask "Which inboxes do I have?" to see them all.
articles.keywords: multiple inboxes several mailboxes accounts which inbox from address switch send as alias
steps: Name the address, for example: "Reply from sales@ to Anna's last email."
Send from an alias Gmail has verified, or one added under Send As addresses.
Missing an inbox? Check that key's Inbox access under API keys.
Free connects one mailbox, Personal three, Pro up to 10 and Business 10 or more.

articles.title: Use the built-in email routines
articles.summary: Some AI clients list ready-made MCPEmails routines. They run only when you start them.
articles.keywords: routines prompts triage follow-up morning brief decisions clean up reply drafts scheduled sends
steps: Look in your AI client's prompt or command menu. Not every client shows them.
Morning inbox triage ranks recent unread mail without changing anything.
Follow-up radar finds conversations where a reply is owed.
Prepare reply drafts writes drafts for you to review.
Clean up safely proposes a plan before changing anything.
